item.title: ServiceTitan
item.description:
ServiceTitan is built for home service trades. Call center staff book jobs, dispatchers assign technicians, technicians use a mobile app to quote and invoice with good-better-best pricing, and the office tracks job costs, marketing, and payroll. Everything ties to one customer record.

Data and AI help companies grow. Tools score inbound calls, flag missed opportunities, recommend pricing, and predict technician performance, and agents assist with booking and follow-ups. Reporting shows revenue per technician and marketing return.

item.title: ActiveCampaign AI
item.description:
ActiveCampaign is built around automation. You design customer journeys that react to behavior: someone joins a list, visits a page, abandons a cart, or opens an email, and the system sends the right follow-up at the right time. Segmentation, split testing, site tracking, and a built-in CRM let small and mid-sized businesses personalize campaigns without a large marketing team. It is common in e-commerce, services, and B2B companies.

Its AI tools help build and manage those journeys. Active Intelligence can audit an account, draft campaigns and automations from a short description, flag automations that are broken or underperforming, and answer questions about results in plain language. Predictive features estimate the best time to send, how likely a contact is to buy, and which deals are most likely to close. A content assistant writes subject lines and email copy.

item.title: Acuity Scheduling
item.description:
Acuity Scheduling lets people book time with you through a branded page that you can link to or embed on a website. It syncs with Google, Outlook, and iCloud calendars so you never get double-booked, and clients pick from available slots in their own time zone. It is used by coaches, therapists, tutors, salons, consultants, and other service providers who sell appointments or classes.

Beyond booking, it handles the admin around an appointment. Clients can fill out custom intake forms, pay deposits or full fees, buy packages and gift certificates, and use coupons. Automatic email and text reminders reduce no-shows, and clients can reschedule themselves. Group classes, multiple staff calendars, and multiple locations are supported on higher plans. Integrations connect to Zoom, Stripe, PayPal, QuickBooks, and Zapier.

item.title: AI-Writer
item.description:
AI-Writer takes a different approach from many article generators. You provide a headline and optional keywords, and it creates a full-length article that pulls in information from sources it finds and cites them, so the draft includes references you can check. This responds to a common complaint about AI writing, which is that it makes claims without support.

Additional features support content marketing. It offers SEO analysis to guide the article toward relevant terms, a built-in indicator that shows how much of the text is verifiable against its sources, and tools for creating outlines, rewriting, and summarizing. The tool is aimed at bloggers, affiliate marketers, and agencies that publish many articles.

item.title: Ajelix
item.description:
Ajelix is built for people who struggle with spreadsheet formulas. You describe what you want, such as the sum of sales in a region for a given month, and it produces the formula along with an explanation, so you can learn as you go. In reverse, you can paste a complicated formula and get a step-by-step explanation in plain language, which is useful when inheriting someone else’s workbook.

It also covers related tasks. Generators can write Google Apps Script and VBA macros from descriptions, convert formulas between Excel and Google Sheets, and assist with SQL queries. An analysis feature lets you upload a file and ask questions to create charts and summaries. The tools are available on the web and as add-ons for spreadsheet apps.

item.title: Amazon CodeWhisperer
item.description:
CodeWhisperer was Amazon’s first coding assistant, a counterpart to GitHub Copilot that suggested lines and whole functions as you typed in editors such as VS Code and the JetBrains IDEs. It was trained with a special focus on AWS APIs, so it was particularly good at code that called S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, and other AWS services. It also supported many popular programming languages.

Two features set it apart from early rivals. A reference tracker flagged suggestions that resembled open-source code and showed the license, and a security scan checked your code for vulnerabilities such as exposed credentials and injection flaws. An individual tier was free, and a professional tier added admin controls and higher limits.

item.title: Amplenote
item.description:
Amplenote treats notes and tasks as part of the same system. You write notes with a Markdown-like editor, link them together, and embed tasks that appear both in the note and in a central task list and calendar. Daily jots capture quick thoughts, and the calendar shows tasks and events alongside notes, so planning the day and recording information happen in one place.

Its task score is an unusual feature: each task gets a number based on its importance, urgency, and effort, and the app highlights the highest-scoring tasks so you know where to begin. A plugin system lets users extend the app with scripts, including features that connect to outside tools. The built-in AI assistant can summarize notes, brainstorm, rewrite text, and use the contents of your notes as context, and it works on web, mobile, and desktop.

item.title: AnythingLLM
item.description:
AnythingLLM gives you a private place to talk to your files. You add documents, web pages, or other content to a workspace, and the app indexes them in a vector database. When you ask a question, it retrieves relevant passages and sends them to a language model, which answers with references.

Flexibility is the main draw. You can choose a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, or a cloud model from providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, and swap them without rebuilding your workspace. It has agents that can browse the web or run tools, supports multiple users and permissions in the server version, and offers an API and embeddable chat widget.

item.title: Anytype
item.description:
Anytype is a workspace for notes and structured information built around privacy. Data is stored locally and encrypted, and syncs between devices peer to peer or through backup nodes, so you keep ownership of your content rather than leaving it on a company server. The app is open source.

Its model uses objects and types. Everything is an object, such as a page, a person, a book, or a task, and each type has fields. Objects link to each other and appear in sets and collections, which function like databases. This lets users create a personal wiki or a custom organizer without code. Optional AI features can summarize and help write.

item.title: Article Forge
item.description:
Article Forge is one of the older AI article generators. You enter a keyword and optionally subtopics, and it produces a long article with headings, sections, and optionally images and videos, in a few minutes. It was designed for people who publish a lot of content, such as affiliate sites, small business blogs, and agencies that manage many clients.

Further tools support publishing. A built-in scheduler can post articles to WordPress automatically, an uniqueness check helps avoid duplicate content, and options control article length, language, and tone. A rewriting function can adjust text, and API access lets developers integrate generation into other systems.

item.title: Asana
item.description:
Asana helps teams keep track of who is doing what by when. Work is organized into projects and tasks, viewable as lists, boards, timelines, or calendars, with dependencies, owners, due dates, and custom fields. Goals connect daily tasks to company objectives, and portfolios give leaders an overview of many projects.

AI features reduce the overhead of managing work. They can generate project plans from a description, summarize updates and conversations, answer questions about project status, and spot risks to deadlines. Asana has also introduced AI teammates that can be assigned work and operate inside projects, with controls to keep humans in charge. Automations handle routing and reminders.

item.title: Asana
item.description: Asana organizes work as tasks inside projects. Each task has an owner, a due date, and a place in a larger plan, and the same project can be viewed as a list, a kanban board, a timeline, or a calendar. Teams use it for campaign planning, product launches, client work, and operations requests, anywhere several people need to see who is doing what and by when. Portfolios and Goals roll individual projects up into a view managers can read without opening every one.

item.title: AutoCrit
item.description:
AutoCrit is an editing tool for novelists. A writer pastes in a chapter or uploads a manuscript, and the software reports on things editors look for: repeated words and phrases, adverbs, filter words, clichés, sentence variety, and dialogue. Reports highlight the text so you can see where to revise.

Its distinctive feature is comparison with published fiction. It measures a manuscript against patterns from successful books in the same genre, such as pacing and the balance of dialogue and description, so a writer can see how their draft differs. Generative features offer suggestions on revision and brainstorming, and a library of guides helps with craft.

item.title: Avoma
item.description: Avoma joins sales, customer success, and recruiting meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then records and transcribes them and produces notes organized by meeting type. Instead of a generic summary, it uses templates suited to the call, such as a discovery call or a customer check-in, and pulls out action items, objections, and next steps. Notes and key fields can be pushed into CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot, which saves reps from doing data entry after every call.

item.title: Beautiful.ai
item.description:
Beautiful.ai tackles a common complaint about PowerPoint: you spend more time fiddling with alignment than thinking about content. Its slides are built from smart templates that rearrange themselves when you add or remove text, images, or chart elements, so the design stays clean. Rules keep spacing, fonts, and colors consistent, and a library of layouts covers timelines, comparisons, charts, team slides, and more.

AI features help create the first draft. You can describe a presentation, or paste in notes, and it generates an outline and slides in the app’s format, which you then edit. Teams can store brand colors, fonts, and logos in a shared theme, share slide libraries, and collaborate on decks with comments. Presentations can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, or shared by link with view analytics.

item.title: Bito AI
item.description:
Bito started as a chat and code-completion assistant inside VS Code and JetBrains IDEs and as a command-line tool. You could ask it to explain a function, write unit tests, find bugs, or generate documentation, and it used a model of your choice for the answers. Its early appeal was practical convenience: reusable prompts for common tasks and support for working with context from your project.

The product has increasingly centered on code review. The AI Code Review Agent examines pull requests on GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket, leaves comments on issues such as bugs, security problems, and style violations, and summarizes the change for reviewers. It builds a model of the codebase so its feedback accounts for how the changed code fits with the rest, which helps reduce noisy comments. Teams use it to speed up reviews and catch issues earlier.

item.title: Blackbox AI
item.description: Blackbox AI was built for programmers. It offers code completion, a chat interface for coding questions, code search, and the ability to turn a screenshot or image into code. A VS Code extension and a web app made it easy to try, and the free tier helped it reach a large number of developers. Users ask it to explain unfamiliar code, convert code between languages, write functions, and fix errors.

item.title: Boomerang
item.description: Boomerang adds time management to Gmail and Outlook. You can write an email and schedule it to send later, set a message to return to your inbox if nobody replies by a certain date, or hide an email until the moment you want to deal with it. Recurring messages, read receipts, and a pause feature that holds incoming mail until you choose to see it help people manage busy inboxes.

item.title: Brave Leo
item.description: Leo sits in the browser’s sidebar and works with whatever page you are viewing. You can ask it to summarize an article or a long video transcript, explain a technical passage, extract key points from a PDF, or answer questions about the content, without copying text into a separate chatbot. It can also help write or rewrite text, translate, brainstorm, and answer general questions, with the option of using the web for current information.

item.title: Brevo AI
item.description:
Brevo started as an email marketing service called Sendinblue and has expanded into a broader customer engagement suite. It covers email and SMS campaigns, WhatsApp messaging, transactional email for apps, landing pages, forms, live chat, and a CRM for sales pipelines. Automation workflows send messages based on behavior, such as a signup or abandoned cart, and segmentation lets marketers target the right audience.

AI features support content and timing. A writing assistant drafts subject lines and email copy, generates images, and adjusts tone, while send-time optimization picks the best time to reach each contact. Predictive tools estimate engagement, and AI chat features help with customer conversations. The product is positioned for small and mid-sized businesses that want many channels in one tool at a reasonable price.

item.title: Calendly
item.description:
Calendly removes the back-and-forth of finding a meeting time. You connect your calendar, set the hours you are available and the types of meetings you offer, and share a link. Invitees choose a slot in their own time zone, and the event appears on both calendars with a video link added automatically. Buffers, meeting limits, and minimum notice settings keep the schedule manageable.

Teams use more advanced features. Round-robin scheduling spreads meetings across several people, collective events find times when everyone is free, and routing forms send prospects to the right person based on their answers. Workflows send reminders and follow-ups, payments can be collected through Stripe or PayPal, and integrations connect with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Salesforce, HubSpot, and Slack. Newer AI features help with note-taking and scheduling assistance.

item.title: ChatGPT Canvas
item.description:
Canvas changes how you work with ChatGPT on longer projects. When a request involves writing a document or code, ChatGPT can open a separate pane next to the conversation, where the text or code appears as an editable file. You can edit it directly, highlight a passage and ask ChatGPT to change just that part, and see changes without the whole response being regenerated.

For writing, shortcuts adjust the length, reading level, and tone, add polish or emojis, and suggest edits inline like a collaborator leaving comments. For coding, Canvas helps review code, add comments and logs, fix bugs, and port a project to another language, and it can run some code, such as Python, within the interface. Version history lets you go back to earlier drafts.

item.title: Chibi AI
item.description:
Chibi AI aims to support writers who produce longer pieces. It provides a clean editor where you can draft with AI help, continue a passage, rewrite sections, and adjust tone or length, with a focus on staying in the flow of writing instead of juggling templates. The tool is aimed at bloggers, students, and fiction writers who want a collaborator that suggests next paragraphs or alternative phrasing.

It offers features common to AI writing tools, such as outline generation, summarizing, expanding ideas, and fixing grammar, with options to guide the style. Users can save projects and export their writing. The simple interface keeps focus on the text instead of a long menu of tools.

item.title: Claap
item.description: Claap targets teams that want fewer live meetings. You can record your screen and camera as a short video, share a link, and let colleagues watch and respond on their own time. The same tool records live calls on Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then stores them with a transcript. Comments and reactions can be attached to specific moments, so feedback stays tied to the part of the video it refers to.

item.title: Claude Code
item.description: Claude Code works as an agent on your actual project instead of a suggestion engine in an editor. You start it in a repository from the terminal and describe the task, such as fixing a failing test, adding an endpoint, or upgrading a dependency. It reads the relevant files, makes a plan, edits code across the project, runs tests and other commands, and iterates on the errors. It asks permission for actions that could be risky, and you can review changes as diffs or through git before committing.

item.title: Clickup
item.description: ClickUp tries to be a single home for everything a team does. At its center are tasks that can be shown as lists, boards, calendars, Gantt charts, or timelines, and each task can have subtasks, custom fields, dependencies, and checklists. Around that sit docs, wikis, whiteboards, forms, dashboards, goals, and built-in chat. Teams use it for software sprints, marketing calendars, client projects, and operations, and the same workspace can be shaped differently for each department.

item.title: Clockwise
item.description:
Clockwise worked inside Google Calendar and Slack to protect time for deep work. It looked at a team’s calendars, moved flexible meetings, and combined scattered gaps into longer blocks, aiming to cut the constant switching between tasks that fragments a workday. It could also find meeting times that worked for groups.

The product grew a following among engineering and product teams, and added AI scheduling features and a way to plan work around priorities. The company ended the service and the team joined Salesforce, where they work on AI agents. The product itself did not move over.

item.title: Coda AI
item.description:
Coda reimagines the document as something that can behave like an app. A Coda doc can contain text, tables, buttons, and automations, so a team can build a project tracker, a wiki, a CRM, or a planning tool in the same document where they write. Formulas, similar to those in spreadsheets, connect data across the doc, and Packs integrate with outside services such as Slack, Jira, and Google Calendar.

AI features run through the platform. Coda AI can summarize documents, draft text, fill table columns with generated content, categorize and extract information, and answer questions about the contents of a doc. AI blocks and agents can be placed in workflows to automate tasks. The company joined Grammarly, which has taken the name Superhuman, and its tools are being combined with Grammarly’s writing assistant and the Superhuman email app.

item.title: Codeium
item.description: Codeium started as a free alternative to GitHub Copilot, offering code completion and chat in more than 40 editors, among them VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Vim, and Neovim. Its free individual tier and wide editor support earned it a large user base among developers who did not want to pay for a coding assistant or switch editors. It added features such as natural-language code search, in-editor chat, and support for dozens of programming languages.

item.title: CodeRabbit
item.description:
CodeRabbit acts as a first reviewer. When a developer opens a pull request, it reads the diff along with surrounding code, writes a summary of the change, and leaves comments on potential bugs, missing tests, security concerns, and style. Developers can reply to its comments and ask it to explain or fix things, so the review becomes a conversation.

Configuration lets teams set rules and instructions in plain language so the review follows their standards. It learns from feedback, and can run linters and security scanners as part of the review. IDE and command line versions bring review earlier, before a pull request is opened.

item.title: CodeRabbit
item.description:
CodeRabbit gives every pull request a quick first review. When a developer opens a pull request, it summarizes the change, walks through the files, and leaves comments on potential bugs, security problems, performance concerns, and deviations from team conventions. It can also suggest fixes that developers apply with a click and answer questions in the comments, acting like a tireless reviewer available at any hour.

It improves with use. CodeRabbit learns from how reviewers respond to its suggestions and from guidelines the team defines, so comments become more relevant over time. It runs linters and security scanners as part of its review, can use context from the wider codebase, and has an IDE and command-line version for reviewing before code is pushed. It integrates with issue trackers to check that changes match requirements.

item.title: Compose AI
item.description:
Compose AI works wherever you type in Chrome. As you write an email or a message, it suggests the next words or sentence, which you accept with a keystroke, similar to code completion in a programming editor. It can also draft whole replies, rewrite text in a different tone, and fix grammar, with a menu of shortcuts for common tasks.

The product came from a startup that focused on autocomplete for writing, and later added generative features that call large language models for longer tasks. It is intended to save keystrokes on repetitive writing such as emails, support replies, and social posts, and to reduce the effort of starting a draft. A free tier covers basic use, with paid plans for more generations and features.

item.title: Content at Scale
item.description:
Content at Scale launched as a tool for generating complete blog posts. You enter a keyword, a URL, or a video, and the system researches the topic and writes a long article designed to read naturally, with sections, headings, and optimization for search. It was marketed on producing content that would pass AI detection and be useful to readers, which made it popular with SEO agencies and publishers.

The company has rebranded to BrandWell and widened its offering. It now describes a platform for brand growth that includes keyword research, content planning, optimization, and generation, with the long-form writer continuing as one of its core tools. Existing customers kept their accounts, and the older name may still appear on some pages or in billing.

item.title: Copy.ai
item.description:
Copy.ai started in the first wave of AI writing tools. You picked a template, such as a product description, email, or social caption, answered a few prompts, and got several drafts to edit. It was popular with marketers and small businesses who needed a lot of copy quickly. Over time it moved away from one-off text generation and toward automating sales and marketing processes.

Its later product centered on workflows. A team could chain steps together, for example researching an account, pulling in data, drafting outreach, and writing a CRM update, and let AI agents run the sequence on a schedule or trigger. A data layer called Tables kept the inputs organized, and the aim was to replace manual go-to-market busywork with repeatable automations rather than just generating paragraphs.

item.title: Craft Docs
item.description: Craft aims to make notes and documents that look good. It works as a block-based editor where text, images, tables, and cards live in nested pages that you can reorganize easily. Native apps for Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch are fast and polished, with offline support, and there is also a web and Windows version. Daily notes and tasks cover personal organization, and Spaces and collections keep larger projects tidy.

item.title: Cursor Composer
item.description: Composer was Cursor’s answer to a basic limit of early AI coding tools, which could suggest a line or edit one file but struggled with changes that touched several. You describe a feature or refactor, and Composer works out which files need to change, writes the edits, and shows them as diffs for you to accept or reject. It can create new files, update imports, and keep related code consistent. The feature later evolved into Cursor’s agent, which also runs commands and fixes its own errors.

item.title: Decktopus
item.description: Decktopus is built for people who need a presentation quickly. You enter a topic or a short brief, answer a few questions about the audience and goal, and the AI produces an outline and a deck of designed slides with suggested images and speaker notes. You then edit the text and layout in a drag-and-drop editor. It also offers templates for pitches, reports, and sales decks, and a brand kit for colors and logos.

item.title: DocuSign AI
item.description:
Docusign made electronic signatures routine. Senders upload a document, specify signers and fields, and recipients sign on any device, with an audit trail and legal validity in many countries. It’s used for sales contracts, HR paperwork, real estate, and any agreement that once needed a pen, and it integrates with Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and many business systems.

The company has expanded to manage the whole agreement lifecycle. Its Intelligent Agreement Management platform includes tools to prepare and negotiate agreements, a repository that stores them, and AI that reads contracts to extract terms such as renewal dates, obligations, and parties. Its AI can summarize documents, answer questions about a contract portfolio, and flag risks, and workflow tools automate steps such as approvals and routing.

item.title: Fathom
item.description: Fathom is known for making meeting notes free. It joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams calls, records them, and creates a transcript in real time. You can highlight important moments during the call with a click, and within seconds of the meeting ending, it produces a summary with decisions, action items, and key points that you can share. The free plan includes unlimited recordings and transcripts, which set it apart from competitors that cap free use.

item.title: Fellow
item.description:
Fellow helps teams run better meetings. Before a meeting, it provides shared agendas and templates for one-on-ones, team meetings, and client calls. During the meeting, an AI notetaker records and transcribes, capturing decisions and action items automatically. Afterward, summaries and tasks are sent to attendees.

The platform keeps a record of conversations over time, which suits managers who run recurring one-on-ones. Integrations connect with calendars, Slack, Zoom, Teams, and project tools. AI features answer questions across past meetings and draft follow-up messages. Feedback tools support regular check-ins and performance conversations.

item.title: Fireflies.ai
item.description: Fireflies sends a bot into your meetings, usually named Fred, that records the call and creates a transcript with speaker labels. After the meeting, it produces a summary with action items and key topics, and posts them where your team works. Every meeting becomes searchable text, so you can find what a customer said last month or when a decision was made. It supports dozens of languages and works with the main video call platforms and uploaded recordings.

item.title: Formula Bot
item.description:
Formula Bot is aimed at spreadsheet users who know what they want but not the syntax. You describe the calculation, such as finding the average of a column when another column equals a value, and it produces the formula with an explanation. It can also explain a formula you paste in and fix errors, which helps when you inherit a workbook full of nested functions.

The tool extends beyond formulas. It can write scripts, SQL queries, and regular expressions from descriptions, convert between formula dialects, and answer questions about data you upload by building charts and summaries. A chat-style data analysis feature lets users ask questions of a spreadsheet and receive results, aimed at people who don’t write formulas at all.

item.title: Gamma
item.description:
Gamma reimagined the presentation. Instead of slides built from a blank template, you describe what you want, such as a pitch for a new product or a lesson on photosynthesis, and Gamma generates a complete, designed deck with text, layouts, and images. The format uses flexible cards that expand and collapse, so presentations can feel more like interactive documents, and it also produces documents and one-page websites.

Editing is conversational and visual. You can ask the AI to rewrite a section, change the style, add images, or restructure, or edit manually with simple controls. Themes keep designs consistent, brand settings apply company fonts and colors, and sharing by link includes analytics on who viewed it. Decks can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, and it integrates with other tools.

item.title: Gemini in Workspace
item.description:
Gemini in Workspace brings Google’s models into the apps people use at work. In Gmail, it drafts replies and summarizes long threads. In Docs, it writes, rewrites, and proofreads, and can pull in information from files and email. In Sheets, it helps create formulas, tables, and analysis. In Slides, it generates slides and images, and in Meet it takes notes and summarizes.

A side panel gives a chat assistant that can search across a user’s Drive, Gmail, and Calendar, and answer questions using that content. Organizations can control access, and Google states that business data is not used to train models without permission. Newer features include agents and tools such as NotebookLM for deeper source work.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Workspace
item.description: Copilot Workspace was GitHub Next’s attempt to rethink how AI fits into the work of fixing an issue. Starting from a GitHub issue or a prompt, it first wrote a specification of the current and desired behavior, then a plan listing the files to change, and finally the code. At each stage, you could edit the text, so you steered the work in plain English before any code appeared. The finished changes could be opened as a pull request or run in a cloud environment.

item.title: Glean
item.description:
Glean addresses the problem that company knowledge lives in dozens of separate tools. It connects to those systems through hundreds of connectors, builds an index of documents, messages, tickets, and other content, and lets employees search across everything from one box. Crucially, it mirrors the permissions of the source systems, so a person only sees results they would already have access to.

On top of search, Glean provides an AI assistant that answers questions in natural language using company information, with citations to the underlying sources. Employees ask things like how a process works, what was decided in a project, or what the latest customer feedback says, and receive a synthesized answer. Glean Agents let teams build automations and agents that take actions in connected apps, and a builder allows non-engineers to create them. Companies can choose among language models from several providers.

item.title: Google Assistant
item.description: Google Assistant is the voice assistant that ships on Android phones, Nest speakers and displays, Android Auto, Wear OS watches, and many third-party smart home devices. You wake it with a phrase or a button, then ask it to set a timer, add a calendar event, send a message, play music, or turn off the lights. It works well for short, concrete commands, and a large ecosystem of smart home brands supports it, which made it one of the more capable options for controlling a connected home.

item.title: Google Jules
item.description:
Jules is designed for the delegating style of AI-assisted coding. You link a GitHub repository, describe a task, and Jules makes a plan, works in a secure cloud virtual machine, and proposes changes while you do something else. It clones the repository, installs dependencies, writes code, runs tests, and presents the plan and results for your review. When you approve, it opens a pull request.

It handles routine, well-defined jobs such as bug fixes, adding tests, upgrading dependencies, updating documentation, and implementing small features. You can run several tasks in parallel, review the plan before it starts, and give feedback while it is working. It is powered by Google’s Gemini models and integrates with GitHub issues and the command line.

item.title: GPT Engineer
item.description:
GPT Engineer was among the first projects to show that a language model could generate a whole working program from a prompt. A user wrote a specification, the tool asked clarifying questions, and then it produced files and code. The open-source command line version attracted a large community of developers.

The founders built a hosted product, gptengineer.app, that let non-programmers describe a web app and see it built. That product was renamed Lovable, which grew into one of the best-known AI app builders. The original open-source repository remains available as a way to experiment with prompt-to-code workflows.

item.title: Grain
item.description:
Grain records meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and other platforms and turns them into transcripts, summaries, and short clips. Its clip feature is a distinguishing idea: instead of sharing a whole recording, you highlight a moment, such as a customer’s feedback or a question about pricing, and share just that clip with colleagues. This makes customer insights easier to spread across product, marketing, and leadership.

AI features produce structured notes from each meeting using templates, such as discovery calls or customer interviews, and answer questions across a library of recordings. Integrations send notes and fields to Salesforce, HubSpot, Notion, and Slack, which cuts manual updates. A desktop capture option can record meetings without a visible bot joining the call, which some teams prefer for external meetings.

item.title: Grammarly
item.description:
Grammarly started as a grammar checker and became the writing helper people keep installed everywhere. A browser extension, desktop app, mobile keyboard, and plugins for Word and Google Docs underline mistakes in emails, messages, and documents as you type. It catches typos and grammar errors, flags wordy or unclear sentences, and suggests a different tone, such as more confident or more friendly. A free version covers the basics.

Generative AI is built into the same flow. You can ask it to rewrite a paragraph, shorten a message, draft a reply to an email, or brainstorm ideas from a prompt. AI agents focus on particular jobs, such as giving feedback on a student paper, predicting how a reader might respond, or checking citations. Paid tiers add full-sentence rewrites, tone detection, plagiarism checking, and an AI detector, and business plans add style guides, brand tone, and analytics for teams.

item.title: Height
item.description: Height set out to make project management less manual. It was a task and project tracker with a clean interface, and its main idea was that AI should do routine upkeep: sorting incoming requests, writing and updating subtasks, assigning work, and keeping descriptions consistent. Teams used it as a lighter alternative to Jira with more automation, and the product drew fans among startups for its design and its early AI features.

item.title: Heptabase
item.description: Heptabase treats notes as cards that you place on whiteboards, group, and connect. Instead of a long document or a folder tree, you build up an understanding of a topic visually: a card for each idea, laid out next to related ones, with arrows and sections that show structure. It suits people who learn and plan by seeing the relationships among ideas, such as researchers, students, writers, and product thinkers.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description: HubSpot started as a marketing software company and grew into a full platform for managing the customer relationship from first visit to renewal. It is organized into hubs: Marketing Hub for email, forms, ads, and landing pages, Sales Hub for pipelines and sequences, Service Hub for tickets and help desk, Content Hub for websites and blogs, and Operations Hub for data syncing and automation. All of them read from the same CRM, so a marketer, a sales rep, and a support agent are looking at one record of the customer.

item.title: INK Editor
item.description:
INK combines an editor with optimization guidance. As you write an article, the tool analyzes the search results for your target keyword and gives a score that reflects how well you cover the topic, which terms to include, and how readable the piece is. Suggestions appear in the sidebar, so you can improve the draft while writing instead of editing afterward.

AI features generate text and help overcome writer’s block. You can ask for outlines, introductions, and rewritten paragraphs, and use a plagiarism checker and content shield tools to monitor originality. The product works in a web editor and has extensions for common platforms, and teams can collaborate on content.

item.title: Jasper
item.description: Jasper was one of the first dedicated AI writing products and has focused on marketing teams that need a lot of on-brand content. You describe what you need, such as a product launch email or a set of ad variations, and it drafts the copy using your guidelines. Brand Voice learns your tone from sample content, and a knowledge base stores product details, audiences, and approved messaging, so output needs fewer corrections.

item.title: Jenni AI
item.description:
Jenni AI is designed around the way academics write. In its editor, you start a document and Jenni suggests how to continue sentences, offers to expand or rephrase text, and helps structure arguments. It can generate an outline from a topic and help draft sections, with the writer keeping control and deciding what to accept.

Research features distinguish it from general writing tools. You can search for academic sources, insert citations in styles such as APA and MLA, and manage a bibliography. A feature lets you upload PDFs and ask questions about them, so you can use sources more efficiently. The tool also supports different citation formats and exports to common document formats.

item.title: Klaviyo AI
item.description:
Klaviyo is built on the idea that a store’s own customer data is the best basis for marketing. It connects to platforms like Shopify, BigCommerce, and WooCommerce, pulling in orders, browsing behavior, and product information. Marketers build segments, such as customers who bought twice in the last 60 days, and send targeted email and SMS campaigns and automated flows, like abandoned cart reminders, welcome series, and post-purchase follow-ups.

AI adds prediction and automation. Klaviyo estimates a customer’s likelihood to buy again, expected lifetime value, and probable next order date, and uses those signals for segmentation. Product recommendations personalize emails, send-time optimization chooses delivery times, and generative tools write subject lines and campaign copy and build flows from a description. A customer hub, reviews, and a CDP add other parts of the retention workflow.

item.title: Koala AI
item.description: Koala focuses on creating articles that are designed to rank. You enter a keyword, and the tool analyzes current search results, collects information from the web, and writes a structured article with headings, optional images, and links. It supports one-click generation of long pieces, and special modes for product reviews, listicles, and how-to guides. Real-time data is meant to keep information fresh compared with models that only use training data.

item.title: LanguageTool
item.description:
LanguageTool checks writing for spelling, grammar, punctuation, and style, and is notable for its broad language support, including English, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, Portuguese, and many more. It runs as browser extensions, add-ins for Microsoft Word and Google Docs, a desktop app, and an API, so it can check text wherever you write. Many people use it for writing in a second language or switching between languages.

The core engine is open source and can be self-hosted, which appeals to organizations with privacy requirements and to developers who want to integrate a checker. The premium tier adds more advanced style suggestions, tone and clarity feedback, and AI-powered rephrasing, along with higher character limits. Teams can set custom dictionaries and style rules.

item.title: Lex
item.description:
Lex is a document editor with AI woven in. The interface is clean and focused on writing, and the AI helps in small ways: continuing a thought when you are stuck, offering alternative phrasings, and giving feedback on drafts. Users keep control, and the tool tries not to replace their voice.

Features include a way to ask for critique, suggestions for headlines and next paragraphs, and the ability to have the AI respond to your own text in a side conversation. Writers use it for essays, newsletters, and notes where they want a thinking partner rather than automatic content.

item.title: Linear
item.description: Linear is a project management tool aimed at product and engineering teams. Its pitch is that the tool should get out of your way: pages load instantly, nearly everything can be done from the keyboard, and the data model is opinionated about how software gets built. Work is tracked as issues, grouped into cycles (time-boxed sprints), projects, and initiatives, with roadmaps on top for the longer view. Many teams switch to it from Jira because there is far less configuration to maintain.

item.title: Liner
item.description:
Liner started as a tool for highlighting text on web pages and saving it. Users mark passages in articles and PDFs, which are collected and organized, so they can find them later. A browser extension and app make highlighting part of normal browsing.

AI features add search and summaries. An AI search engine returns answers with sources and surfaces relevant parts of highlighted content, and tools summarize pages and documents. A chat assistant answers questions about what a user is reading. It is popular with students and researchers, particularly in Korea where the company began.

item.title: LongShot AI
item.description:
LongShot AI is aimed at publishers and marketers who want blog posts with fewer unsupported claims. You provide a topic or keyword, and the tool researches the web and writes a structured article, with options to cite sources and run fact checks against search results. It can generate outlines, intros, and full drafts, and has a workspace for editing.

Additional features help with the content workflow. An SEO assistant suggests keywords and optimization steps, a rewrite tool paraphrases and adjusts tone, and a calendar helps plan publishing. Teams can collaborate in the editor, and templates cover common formats such as product reviews, how-to articles, and listicles. Users range from solo bloggers to small agencies.

item.title: Make
item.description: Make, formerly called Integromat, lets you automate work between apps by drawing it. You place modules on a canvas for each app, such as Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, or a CRM, and connect them with lines that show how data flows. You can add routers that split the flow into branches, filters that decide which items continue, iterators that handle lists, and functions that change data on the way. This visual layout makes complicated logic easier to follow than a long linear list of steps.

item.title: MarketMan
item.description:
MarketMan is back-of-house software for food service. Operators record what they buy and use, build recipes with ingredient costs, and see the cost of each dish. When prices change or usage varies, the system flags it, helping managers protect margins.

Ordering and invoicing are handled in one place. Staff place orders with suppliers, receive deliveries, and match invoices to what arrived, which catches errors and short shipments. Forecasting tools predict how much to order based on sales history, and integrations connect with point of sale and accounting systems.

item.title: MeetGeek
item.description:
MeetGeek joins your calendar’s online meetings, records them, and produces a transcript and summary after each one. The summary lists decisions, action items, and key points, and highlights flag important moments. Notes are sent automatically to attendees or to tools like Slack, Notion, HubSpot, and Google Docs, which cuts down on manual write-ups.

Beyond a single meeting, it organizes knowledge across your calls. Hubs group meetings by team or topic, and you can search past conversations or ask questions about them. Meeting templates tailor summaries for sales calls, interviews, or team check-ins, and analytics show participation and talk time. Teams can get insights into patterns across customer calls.

item.title: Meta AI
item.description: Meta AI is the assistant that Meta put where its users already are. In WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, and Facebook, you can mention it in a chat or open it from the search bar to ask a question, get recommendations, or generate an image. There is also a standalone app and website with fuller features, including natural voice conversations, image creation and editing, and a feed where people share what they have made.

item.title: Microsoft Power Automate
item.description:
Power Automate connects apps and automates repetitive work. Users build flows that trigger on events, such as an email arriving or a form submission, and perform actions in hundreds of services. It works smoothly with Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, and Dynamics.

AI features extend it. Copilot lets people describe a flow in plain language, AI Builder processes documents and forms, and agent capabilities handle more open-ended tasks. Desktop flows use robotic process automation to control applications that have no API.

item.title: Microsoft Power Automate
item.description:
Power Automate helps people automate repetitive work without code. In a visual designer, users create flows that start from a trigger, such as an email arriving or a form being submitted, and then run actions like saving attachments, updating a spreadsheet, sending approvals, or posting to Teams. It connects to hundreds of services, with deep integration with SharePoint, Outlook, Excel, and Dynamics 365, and handles scheduled and event-driven tasks.

It also covers robotic process automation. Desktop flows record and replay actions on a computer, allowing automation of legacy applications that lack APIs. AI Builder adds capabilities such as reading text from documents, classifying content, and making predictions, and Copilot can build a flow from a plain-language description. Newer features support AI agents that use flows as tools.

item.title: Miro AI
item.description:
Miro provides an infinite shared canvas where teams place sticky notes, diagrams, documents, and images, and work together live or asynchronously. It’s used for brainstorming, retrospectives, user journey maps, roadmaps, and workshops, particularly for distributed teams. A large library of templates, integrations with tools such as Jira, Slack, and Google Drive, and facilitation features like timers and voting make it versatile.

AI features speed up creation and synthesis. Users can generate diagrams, flowcharts, and mind maps from a prompt, summarize and cluster hundreds of sticky notes into themes, and turn a board into a document or a prototype. Sidekicks are AI helpers with specific roles, such as a product manager or a retrospective facilitator, that give feedback and suggestions on the board. Flows connect several AI steps for repeatable processes.

item.title: Mixmax
item.description:
Mixmax turns Gmail into a sales workspace. It tracks opens, clicks, and replies, lets you schedule messages, and adds a calendar tool so recipients can book meetings from your email. Templates and snippets speed up repetitive writing, and polls, surveys, and documents can be embedded. It is used by sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that live in their inbox.

Sequences are a main feature: automated multi-step email campaigns that send follow-ups until someone replies, with rules for pausing and routing. Integrations connect with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach alternatives, Slack, and Zapier, so activity is logged in the CRM. AI helps draft emails, personalize at scale, and suggest next steps, and call recording and meeting notes have been added in some plans.

item.title: Monday.com
item.description:
Monday.com organizes work in colorful boards that resemble spreadsheets. Teams track projects, sales pipelines, marketing campaigns, and operations with columns for status, owners, dates, and more, and view the same data as a timeline, calendar, or chart. No-code automations handle routine updates and notifications.

The platform has expanded into products for sales CRM, service desks, and software development, built on the same foundation. AI assistants create boards from a description, summarize items and updates, write content, and extract information, and agents can take on tasks within workflows.

item.title: Motion
item.description: Motion tries to take planning off your hands. You add tasks with deadlines, durations, and priorities, connect your calendar, and Motion places each task into open time on your calendar. If a meeting gets added or a task runs long, it rebuilds the schedule automatically so you always see a realistic plan for the day. The goal is to protect focus time and make sure deadlines are met without constant manual rearranging.

item.title: Mutable AI
item.description:
Mutable AI was a startup building AI tools for programmers. Its VS Code extension offered code completion, refactoring, and chat that could answer questions about a project, and its AutoPilot feature aimed to carry out a described feature across a codebase. The team later became known for turning repositories into readable, wiki-style documentation, which helps developers understand unfamiliar code.

Google acquired the company, and the original Mutable AI site no longer works. The idea of generating a living wiki for a codebase continues in Google’s own products, where documentation tools built on that concept have appeared. Users of the earlier extension needed to move to other assistants, as the standalone service is gone.

item.title: n8n
item.description: n8n lets you build automations by connecting nodes on a canvas, similar to Zapier or Make, but with more room for code. Each node is a step: a trigger like a webhook or schedule, an action in an app, or a block that transforms data with JavaScript or Python. Hundreds of integrations are included, and a generic HTTP node covers the rest. Workflows can branch, loop, and call other workflows, so it handles anything from simple notifications to elaborate data pipelines.

item.title: Narrato
item.description:
Narrato helps teams manage the whole content process. A content calendar plans what to publish, assignments route work to writers and editors, and approval workflows track progress. The AI writer generates drafts, outlines, social posts, and ad copy in a team’s style, and SEO tools provide keyword suggestions and optimization scores.

Additional tools address agencies and publishers. Brief generation creates instructions for writers, a plagiarism checker and AI content detector help check originality, and a marketplace lets teams hire freelance writers for content that needs a human touch. Integrations publish directly to WordPress and other platforms, and an AI assistant helps with ideas and repurposing.

item.title: Nintex
item.description:
Nintex helps organizations digitize their processes. Using a visual designer, business analysts build workflows that route requests, collect approvals, update systems, and send notifications, and they create forms to start those workflows. It integrates with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Salesforce, and many other systems, which is where its roots lie, with many customers automating processes on SharePoint.

The platform has several parts. Process mapping tools document how work actually happens, automation tools execute workflows and robotic process automation, and document generation tools produce contracts and reports from data. AI features assist with building workflows from descriptions and extracting data from documents, and analytics show where processes slow down.

item.title: Notion
item.description:
Notion lets people build their own workspace from simple pieces. A page can hold text, headings, checklists, images, embedded files, and databases, and databases can be shown as tables, boards, calendars, or galleries. Teams use it for wikis, meeting notes, project tracking, product roadmaps, and personal organization, and templates help people get started. Real-time collaboration, comments, and permissions make it work for teams as well as individuals.

The product has grown beyond notes. Notion Calendar and Notion Mail connect scheduling and email to the workspace, and Sites turns pages into public web pages. Notion AI adds writing help, summaries, translation, and question answering across your workspace and connected tools like Slack and Google Drive, plus agents that perform tasks. AI meeting notes capture and summarize calls. See the Notion AI entry for details on those features.

item.title: Noty.ai
item.description:
Noty.ai is a lightweight tool for people who want meeting notes without much setup. It records and transcribes online meetings, then creates a summary that highlights the main discussion points, decisions, and tasks. The goal is to let participants focus on the conversation instead of typing, and to give everyone a shared record afterward.

Its integrations make the notes easy to reuse. Summaries can be pushed to Notion and other workspace tools, and the transcript is searchable, so you can find what was said about a topic in a past meeting. A browser extension handles recording in Google Meet and Zoom, and a free plan lets individuals try the product.

item.title: Numerous
item.description:
Numerous brings language models into the spreadsheet. After installing the add-in, you use a formula such as =AI(“prompt”, cell) in a cell to ask the model to do something with the data: categorize customer feedback, write product descriptions, extract names from messy text, translate, or summarize. Filling the formula down a column performs the task on hundreds or thousands of rows, which would take hours by hand.

It aims to be approachable for people who know spreadsheets but not code. Prompts are written in plain language, results appear in cells where you can filter and calculate with them, and features help with common tasks like cleaning, tagging, and brainstorming. Marketers, e-commerce teams, researchers, and operations staff use it to process lists of items quickly.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: Obsidian treats notes as local files. Everything you write is a Markdown document in a folder on your computer, so you own the data and can open it with any other editor. You connect notes with links, and the app shows backlinks and a graph view of how ideas relate. People use it for personal knowledge management, research, writing, journaling, and project notes, and many build large networks of thousands of linked notes over years.

item.title: Originality.ai
item.description:
Originality.ai was built for people who commission or publish written content and want to know whether it was written by AI. You paste text or scan a URL, and it returns a score estimating the likelihood the text was generated by models such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, alongside a plagiarism check against web sources. Content teams, SEO agencies, and website buyers use it to check contractors’ work.

Additional tools include a fact-checking aid, a readability analysis, and a feature that shows the writing history of a Google Doc to demonstrate how it was composed. A Chrome extension and API support integration with publishing workflows, and team accounts allow reviewing many pieces. The company publishes accuracy studies, although its results are disputed by others.

item.title: Otter.ai
item.description: Otter was one of the first widely used meeting transcription tools. You connect your calendar, and its assistant joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Teams calls to record, transcribe, and label speakers. The transcript is available live, so participants can follow along, and afterward you get a summary, key points, and action items. Everything is searchable, so you can find what was said in a past meeting by keyword. It also works on phones for in-person conversations and lectures.

item.title: PandaDoc AI
item.description:
PandaDoc helps sales teams close deals faster. Users build proposals and quotes from templates in a drag-and-drop editor, add pricing tables with live calculations, embed videos and payment links, and send them to clients, who can review and sign electronically. Tracking shows when a document is opened and viewed, so reps know when to follow up.

Automation and integration make it practical for teams. It connects with CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot to populate documents with deal data and update records when documents are signed, offers approval workflows, content libraries, and a payment step. AI features help generate document content from a prompt, summarize contracts, suggest edits, and extract information, speeding up proposal creation.

item.title: Pi
item.description:
Pi was built to be a kind and curious conversational partner instead of a productivity tool. Its responses are short, warm, and conversational, and it often asks follow-up questions, which made it a favorite with people who wanted to talk through ideas, plans, or feelings in a low-pressure setting. It supports voice conversations with several voices, which suits casual use.

Inflection AI, founded by former DeepMind and LinkedIn leaders, launched Pi with the aim of making a personal AI. The company later saw its founders and much of its team join Microsoft, and it pivoted to licensing its models to enterprises. Pi remains online as a free consumer product at pi.ai and in apps, but active development has slowed, and the messaging integrations it once had are gone.

item.title: Pitch
item.description:
Pitch aims to make presentations that look good without wrestling with layouts. It provides modern templates, smart slide types, and a brand-aware design system that keeps a team’s decks consistent. Collaboration works like a shared document: several people edit at once, leave comments, and track versions, which suits startups, agencies, and sales teams that produce decks together.

Distinctive features include presentation analytics and sharing. You can send a deck as a link and see who viewed it and for how long, which is helpful for investor and sales decks, and recordings let you narrate a deck for asynchronous sharing. AI tools generate slide drafts from a prompt, rewrite text, and create visuals, and the platform integrates with tools like Slack, HubSpot, and Google Drive.

item.title: Plus AI
item.description:
Plus AI takes the approach that you shouldn’t have to leave your slide editor to use AI. After installing the add-in in Google Slides or PowerPoint, you describe the presentation you want, and it drafts an outline and slides in the editor, which you can then adjust like any other deck. It can also build from a document, a set of notes, or a web page.

Editing features save time on existing decks. The remix tool can restyle or rework slides, and the rewrite function changes tone or length of text on a slide. It can convert content into a different layout, summarize, and create speaker notes. Because the output is native slides, the file remains fully editable and compatible with company templates and brand assets.

item.title: Proposify
item.description:
Proposify helps agencies and service companies create and send proposals. Teams build templates with sections, pricing tables, and brand styling, assemble a proposal quickly, and send it to clients who can review, comment, and sign electronically. Notifications show when a proposal is opened.

AI features help with writing content and suggest improvements based on what has worked in past proposals. Analytics reveal how long clients spend on each section, informing follow-ups. Integrations connect with CRMs and billing.

item.title: ProWritingAid
item.description:
ProWritingAid is built for writers who want to improve their craft. As well as catching spelling and grammar errors, it generates reports on overused words, sentence length variation, clichés, passive voice, pacing, dialogue, and readability, which editors and novelists use to revise drafts. The detailed feedback is aimed at long-form writing more than quick messages.

It offers integrations with Microsoft Word, Google Docs, Scrivener, and browsers, and includes a plagiarism checker in higher plans. Newer features use AI to rephrase sentences, suggest rewrites, and offer feedback on structure, and writers can set a house style or custom rules. A lifetime purchase option has been a distinguishing choice compared with subscription-only competitors.

item.title: Qodo AI
item.description:
Qodo started as CodiumAI with a focus on tests, and has expanded to quality across the development process. In the IDE, it analyzes a function, understands its behavior, and generates unit tests that cover normal cases, edge cases, and failure modes, which helps developers raise coverage without writing everything by hand. It also offers chat and code suggestions that take the project context into account.

The review side is a major part. Qodo Merge, built on an open-source tool called PR-Agent, comments on pull requests with summaries, potential bugs, security issues, and suggested fixes, and can learn a team’s standards so reviews reflect internal rules. Multi-agent review systems and a context engine aim to understand large codebases, which matters for enterprise teams with many repositories. Integrations cover GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and major IDEs.

item.title: Qwilr
item.description:
Qwilr replaces static PDF proposals with web pages. A seller builds a proposal from blocks, such as text, images, videos, pricing tables, and acceptance sections, and sends a link. Buyers can adjust options in a pricing table, and sign online, which shortens the path to closing.

Analytics show who viewed the page, how long they spent on each section, and when they came back, which guides follow-up. Templates keep branding consistent, and integrations push data into CRMs. AI drafts content from notes and suggests improvements.

item.title: Raycast AI
item.description:
Raycast puts a command bar on your keyboard. Press a hotkey, type a few letters, and you can launch apps, search files, run calculations, manage windows, paste snippets, control music, and use hundreds of extensions that connect to tools such as GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Slack. Power users value how much it can cut mouse use and context switching.

Raycast AI adds chat and commands powered by leading language models. You can ask a question, rewrite selected text, summarize a page, translate, or run custom AI commands from any app, and switch among models from different providers. AI Extensions let the assistant act through extensions, such as creating an issue or checking a calendar, and Model Context Protocol support connects it to more tools. Chats and presets are synced across devices.

item.title: Readwise Reader
item.description:
Reader is a single inbox for things you want to read. You can save web pages, subscribe to newsletters at a dedicated email address, follow RSS feeds, upload PDFs and ebooks, and import videos with transcripts. Everything appears in a clean reading view, with tools for highlighting, tagging, and taking notes, and it works across web, mobile, and browser extensions.

The connection with Readwise makes it more than a reading list. Highlights flow into Readwise, which resurfaces them through spaced repetition so you remember what you read, and exports them to Notion, Obsidian, Roam, and other note apps. Ghostreader is the AI assistant that can summarize a document, define terms, answer questions about it, and generate custom prompts, and it also supports text-to-speech and features for catching up on a backlog.

item.title: RemNote
item.description: RemNote is built for students who want to learn what they write. In a typical note app, notes sit in a folder and are rarely reviewed. In RemNote, you mark terms and definitions inside your notes, and the app turns them into flashcards automatically, then schedules reviews with a spaced repetition algorithm so facts move into long-term memory. Notes are organized in an outline, and each line can link to others, which helps build a connected knowledge base.

item.title: Replika
item.description: Replika is one of the earliest AI companion apps. You create an avatar, choose a name and appearance, and begin chatting. Over time the AI builds a memory of your interests, relationships, and preferences, and the avatar responds in a way that reflects that history. Users talk to it about their day, vent about problems, practice conversations, or just keep company. It offers text chat, voice calls, and an augmented reality mode that places the avatar in your room.

item.title: Roam Research
item.description:
Roam helped popularize networked note-taking. Notes are organized as outlines of bullet blocks, and you link to other pages by typing double brackets. Every link creates a backlink on the page it points to, so you can see everywhere a concept is mentioned. Daily notes serve as a default home for new thoughts, and over time, links build a web of connected ideas without a rigid folder structure.

Its power comes from working at the block level. Any bullet can be referenced or embedded elsewhere, queries pull together blocks that match conditions, and attributes add structured data to notes. A graph view and a plugin ecosystem add visualization and automation, and keyboard-driven editing makes it fast for those who master it. Researchers, writers, and knowledge workers have used it for long-term thinking.

item.title: Salesforce Einstein
item.description:
Einstein brought AI to Salesforce customers well before generative AI became popular. Predictive features score leads and opportunities, forecast revenue, recommend next best actions, and flag at-risk accounts, using each company’s own CRM data. Einstein Discovery finds patterns and suggests what drives outcomes, and bots and analytics features extend the same ideas to service and marketing.

With generative AI, Einstein has expanded to write emails, summarize records and cases, and generate service replies, grounded in customer data and protected by the Einstein Trust Layer, which masks sensitive information and prevents customer data from being used to train outside models. The conversational assistant evolved into Agentforce, which builds autonomous agents on the same foundation, so Einstein now refers to a mix of older predictive features and the generative AI infrastructure.

item.title: SaneBox
item.description:
SaneBox tackles inbox overload without replacing your email app. It connects to your existing account and analyzes your behavior, such as who you reply to and which messages you open, then moves less important mail into a folder called SaneLater. Newsletters, notifications, and cold outreach end up there, and you get a digest to skim when you choose. The important mail stays in your inbox.

Several tools help you stay in control. SaneBlackHole sends unwanted senders away permanently with a single drag, snooze folders let you hide a message until later, and reminders alert you if a recipient has not replied. A Do Not Disturb feature holds mail for a period. Because it works on the server, it functions with Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, Yahoo, and other providers, and on all your devices.

item.title: Sassbook AI
item.description:
Sassbook AI is a small suite of text tools. The AI story writer takes a premise and creates a narrative, with options to continue and steer the plot, aimed at hobby writers and students looking for ideas. Other tools summarize long text into shorter versions, paraphrase passages in different styles, and generate headlines and titles.

The tools work in a browser with a simple interface. Users paste text or enter a prompt, choose settings such as length or style, and get results they can edit. It also includes a plagiarism check and a few utilities for writers. The target audience includes bloggers, students, and casual writers who need quick help.

item.title: Scalenut
item.description:
Scalenut combines SEO research with AI writing. A user enters a keyword, and the platform analyzes search results to suggest topics, questions, and structure, then produces an outline and draft article, optimized for search. A one-click mode called Cruise creates a full article by following the steps of research, outline, and writing automatically.

Other features support content marketing. A keyword planner clusters terms into topics, an optimization score guides edits, and tools help with rewriting, product descriptions, and social content. The platform includes brand voice settings, a plagiarism checker, and a feature for tracking content performance. Teams can collaborate and manage projects in the app.

item.title: Scribbr
item.description:
Scribbr started as a proofreading and thesis editing service and built free tools for students. The citation generator formats references in common styles, the paraphraser rewrites text, and the grammar checker catches errors. A plagiarism checker compares text against sources, and an AI detector estimates machine-written text.

Students use these tools while writing essays and theses. Paid services include human editing by professional editors, which is a differentiator from purely automated tools. Guides explain academic writing topics.

item.title: Sembly AI
item.description:
Sembly joins your online meetings, records them, and produces a transcript with a structured summary. The summary highlights the main points, tasks, decisions, and risks mentioned, so teams can see what needs follow-up without rewatching. It also supports in-person meetings through its mobile app and uploads of audio files, and works in many languages.

Beyond single meetings, Sembly helps organize knowledge. Workspaces and meeting libraries let teams search past conversations and ask questions across them, and templates adjust the notes for different meeting types such as sales calls or interviews. Integrations push summaries and tasks into Slack, Notion, Asana, Jira, HubSpot, and other tools. Analytics track patterns like meeting time and topics.

item.title: ServiceNow
item.description:
ServiceNow began as an IT service management tool and became a general workflow platform for large organizations. Employees and customers submit requests, such as a laptop problem, a payroll question, or a customer complaint, and the platform routes, tracks, and resolves them using defined workflows. Companies use it as a system of record and action across IT operations, HR, legal, security, and customer service.

AI is central to its current strategy. Now Assist adds generative AI to summarize cases, draft replies, and help agents find answers, and AI agents can take on tasks such as triaging incidents and fulfilling requests with minimal human intervention. The company acquired Moveworks, whose employee assistant is intended to become the front door to the platform, and offers tools to govern and monitor agents across the enterprise.

item.title: Sheet+
item.description:
Sheet+ is for spreadsheet users who know what they want but not the syntax. You describe the calculation, such as the total of sales for a region in a given month, and Sheet+ produces the formula with an explanation. You can paste a formula you don’t understand and get a plain-language breakdown, or paste an error and receive suggestions for fixing it.

It extends to related tasks. It can write Google Apps Script automation from a description, generate regular expressions, and create SQL queries, and integrates with Sheets through an add-on so you can work without leaving the spreadsheet. It’s popular with small business owners, analysts, and anyone who finds formulas intimidating.

item.title: Shortwave
item.description:
Shortwave is a Gmail client that rethinks the inbox. Related messages are grouped into threads, newsletters and receipts can be bundled so they do not clutter the main view, and snooze, scheduling, and split inboxes help you process email faster. It works on Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and the web, and connects to your Gmail account.

AI is central. You can ask the assistant questions about your email, such as what a client asked for last month or when a trip was booked, and it searches and answers using your messages. It summarizes long threads, drafts replies in your tone, and can take actions like organizing, labeling, and scheduling. The goal is to cut the time spent finding and writing.

item.title: Siri
item.description: Siri is the assistant that comes with every Apple device. You say “Hey Siri” or hold a button, then ask it to send a message, set a timer, call someone, play music, adjust a setting, or control HomeKit devices. It works across Apple’s hardware, so the same assistant is on your wrist, in your car through CarPlay, and on a smart speaker. Its biggest advantage is how deeply it ties into the system, since it can act on messages, calendars, reminders, and photos without extra setup.

item.title: Slidebean
item.description:
Slidebean separates writing from design. You enter text for each slide in an outline-style editor, choose a slide type such as problem, solution, market, or team, and the software lays it out, selecting fonts, spacing, and graphics so the result looks professional. That means founders can focus on the message and avoid spending hours on layout. AI features help draft slide content and improve wording.

Because it was built for startups, Slidebean adds extras beyond slides. It offers pitch deck templates based on successful funding decks, tools to share decks and see who viewed them, and a financial model builder for projections. The company has also offered pitch deck design and fundraising services for founders who want expert help.

item.title: SlidesAI
item.description:
SlidesAI works inside Google Slides. You paste in text, such as an essay, notes, or an article, or enter a topic, and the add-on creates a set of slides with titles, bullet points, and layout. It lets you pick a presentation style, color theme, and the number of slides, and can add relevant images. The result is a draft that you edit like any other Google Slides deck.

Additional features support content work. It can summarize long text into key points, paraphrase for clarity, and generate text for slides from a prompt. Because the output is a native Slides file, it can be shared, collaborated on, and presented as usual. It’s popular with students, teachers, and professionals who need a quick starting point.

item.title: Smartsheet AI
item.description:
Smartsheet is built around the grid. Teams manage projects, requests, and processes in sheets that look like spreadsheets but add features such as attachments, comments, dependencies, and approvals. The same data can be viewed as a Gantt chart, calendar, board, or form, and reports and dashboards summarize progress for leaders. It’s used for project plans, marketing calendars, intake processes, and portfolio tracking in many large organizations.

Automation and AI reduce manual work. Rules can send alerts, request approvals, or update fields when conditions are met, and AI helps by generating formulas from plain language, summarizing sheets, creating content, and analyzing data to find trends. Newer features allow building workflows and agents with natural language. Integrations connect with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack, Salesforce, and more.

item.title: Sourcegraph Cody
item.description: Cody grew out of Sourcegraph’s code search, which indexes entire repositories and lets developers find and understand code across many projects. That context was its main advantage: instead of guessing from the open file, Cody could draw on the broader codebase to answer questions, write code that matched existing patterns, and explain how parts of a system fit together. It worked in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and the web, with chat, autocomplete, and commands to edit and test code.

item.title: Spark Mail
item.description:
Spark is an email client that works with Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo, and other accounts. Its Smart Inbox sorts messages into categories, putting people and important mail first and keeping newsletters and notifications out of the way. Features such as snooze, send later, follow-up reminders, and quick replies make it faster to process mail, and a unified inbox combines accounts.

Collaboration is a differentiator. Teams can share emails, comment privately on messages, and draft replies together before sending, which suits small teams who handle shared mailboxes. AI features in the paid tier help write and rewrite emails, summarize long threads, and suggest replies, and a feature can search by asking questions. The app is available on Apple devices, Android, and Windows.

item.title: Square
item.description:
Square is known for its card readers and registers. A small business accepts payments in person, online, or by invoice, tracks inventory, and manages staff and payroll from a single account. Hardware ranges from a simple reader to full countertop systems.

Additional services include appointments, loyalty programs, marketing, and small business loans based on sales. AI assistance writes item descriptions, generates insights from sales data, and answers business questions.

Square charges processing fees per transaction and sells hardware, with paid software tiers for advanced features. It has a free plan for basic use. Alternatives include Toast for restaurants, Clover, Shopify POS, Stripe Terminal, and SumUp. Square suits small retail and food businesses.

item.title: Sunsama
item.description:
Sunsama is built around the idea that planning your day deliberately reduces overwhelm. Each morning, a guided ritual walks you through gathering tasks from different sources, choosing what you can realistically do, estimating the time each will take, and placing them on your calendar.
